all_findings.description: Regression detection cleanup in `process_round()` destroys snapshot evidence before the regression-recovery check uses it. The cleanup filter `self._pre_fix_snapshots = [s for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots if round_idx - s["round"] < 2]` removes all snapshots that are old enough to judge (≥2 rounds old). The subsequent regression-recovery check `regression_this_round = any(round_idx - s["round"] >= 2 ... for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots)` then iterates over the already-filtered list, finding nothing. `regression_this_round` is therefore always `False`, `_healthy_rounds_since_regression` always increments, and `_regression_defer` clears after `resolution_hysteresis` rounds regardless of whether the regression actually resolved. The F005 fix intended to prevent permanent latching is defeated — the defer flag now clears unconditionally.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Move the regression-recovery check BEFORE the cleanup, or compute `regression_this_round` from the unfiltered list before pruning:
# Check BEFORE cleanup
old_snapshots = [s for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots if round_idx - s["round"] >= 2]
regression_this_round = any(
    s.get("metrics", {}).get("finding_count", 0) > 0
    and self._get_current_metric("finding_count") < s["metrics"].get("finding_count", 0) * 0.7
    for s in old_snapshots
)
# Then cleanup
self._pre_fix_snapshots = [s for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots if round_idx - s["round"] < 2]

all_findings.description: `_CHAIN_TO_COUNTER` mapping does not bridge per-model pathology keys. Pathology counters for per-model detections use keys like `f"model_failure_{model_id}"`, `f"parser_yield_{model_id}"`, `f"monotonic_decline_{model_id}"`, `f"cpf_spike_{model_id}"`. But the mapping only contains base keys: `"model_failure": "model_failure"`, etc. When `_verify_remediation_outcomes` succeeds for chain key `"model_failure"`, it calls `self._pathology_counts.pop(self._CHAIN_TO_COUNTER.get("model_failure", "model_failure"), None)` — this pops the base key `"model_failure"` from `_pathology_counts`, but the actual stored key is `"model_failure_{model_id}"`. The per-model pathology count is never cleared after successful remediation, so the pathology appears to persist indefinitely. The Run 7b FFF-C fix addressed the chain-to-counter namespace for system-level pathologies but missed the per-model suffix pattern.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
When clearing pathology counts after remediation success/exhaustion, extract the model_id from the remediation state or the original diagnosis evidence and construct the per-model key:
# In _verify_remediation_outcomes, after improved or chain exhaustion:
counter_key = self._CHAIN_TO_COUNTER.get(pathology_key, pathology_key)
# Check for per-model variant
self._pathology_counts.pop(counter_key, None)
# Also clear any per-model suffixed keys matching this pathology
for k in list(self._pathology_counts.keys()):
    if k.startswith(counter_key + "_"):
        self._pathology_counts.pop(k, None)

all_findings.description: `_verify_z3()` in immune_agents.py has a semantically meaningless if/then check. The regex extracts condition text (`if_then.group(1)` and `if_then.group(2)`) but never uses it. Instead, it creates two completely unrelated boolean variables X and Y, asserts X ∧ ¬Y, and checks satisfiability. This is trivially satisfiable for any claim because X and Y have no logical relationship. Every "if/then" finding will receive verdict REJECTED ("SATISFIABLE_COUNTEREXAMPLE") regardless of content. The B-Cell fix for f-string escaping (Run 10) fixed the crash but did not fix the logic — the function now runs without crashing but produces uniformly wrong results for logical claims.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Use the extracted conditions to build actual z3 constraints, or acknowledge this as a stub and return UNCERTAIN instead of a definitive REJECTED:
if if_then:
    # Cannot meaningfully verify arbitrary natural-language if/then
    # without structured constraint extraction
    print("Z3_UNSTRUCTURED: if/then claim requires manual review")

all_findings.description: `apply_diagnosis()` short-circuits three pathology types (`mu_novelty_disagree`, `dispatch_false_positive`, `verification_miscalibration`) with hard-coded handlers that bypass the remediation chain mechanism entirely. These handlers return before the chain lookup code, so no remediation state is set, no outcome verification runs, and chain escalation never occurs. For example, `mu_novelty_disagree` has a two-step chain (prefer_novelty → widen_mu_window), but the hard-coded path only does the equivalent of step 0 and can never escalate to step 1 if step 0 is ineffective. This creates a permanent remediation ceiling for these three pathology types — they receive only one fixed response regardless of persistence.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Remove the three hard-coded special-case blocks and let the normal chain lookup handle them. The existing `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` entries already define the correct step 0 actions. Alternatively, if the direct-fix pattern is retained for performance, set remediation state so outcome verification and escalation still work:
# After the hard-coded adjustment:
self.health_monitor.set_remediation_state(
    pathology_key="mu_novelty_disagree", chain_idx=0,
    applied_round=round_idx, metric_at_apply=self._get_current_metric("mu"),
    target_metric="mu", chain_length=len(self._REMEDIATION_CHAINS["mu_novelty_disagree"]),
)

all_findings.description: `_apply_transform()` returns `None` when the parameter is already at its floor/ceiling (e.g., tau_sim already at 0.3). In `apply_diagnosis()`, `if adjustment:` gates all downstream actions — recording the adjustment, setting remediation state, and enabling outcome verification. When the transform returns None because the parameter is at bounds, no remediation state is set, so the chain never escalates to the next step. The pathology continues firing every round, the same floored step keeps returning None, and the system is stuck in an infinite loop of ineffective no-op remediations with no escalation path.

`_classify_claim()` in immune_agents.py uses `_MATH_PATTERN` as a near-universal catch-all. The pattern includes `[+\-*/^]` which matches any single arithmetic operator character. Virtually every code-bug description contains at least one of these (hyphens in compound words, asterisks in pointer/emphasis, slashes in paths, plus signs in expressions). Since the check order is STATISTICAL → LOGICAL → STRUCTURAL → MATHEMATICAL → CODE_BEHAVIORAL, the MATHEMATICAL branch fires for almost every finding that isn't caught by the first three specific patterns. This misroutes code bug findings to the B-Cell (SymPy/z3) instead of the CT-Cell (code FFF with source reading). The CT-Cell, which is the only cell capable of reading actual source files, never sees the majority of findings.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Tighten `_MATH_PATTERN` to require mathematical context (e.g., equations between identifiers, explicit formula references) rather than bare operator characters. Move the CODE_BEHAVIORAL default above MATHEMATICAL, or require MATHEMATICAL to match a more specific pattern like `r'\b\w+\s*[=<>]=?\s*\w+\s*[+\-*/^]'`:
_MATH_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"(?:"
    r"\b\w+\s*[=<>!]=\s*\w+"     # comparisons between identifiers
    r"|\bformula\b|\bequation\b|\binequality\b|\bbound\b"
    r"|\bEq\(|\bGt\(|\bLt\("     # SymPy function calls
    r"|\bsqrt\b|\blog\b|\bexp\b" # math functions in context
    r")"
)

all_findings.description: The `prefer_novelty` transform in `_apply_transform()` sets `hm._prefer_novelty_over_mu = True` on the health monitor, but no code path anywhere reads this attribute. The FSM's `select_event()`, the convergence detector's `converged()`, and the diminishing returns detector's `stop()` all ignore it. The remediation has zero effect — it's a dead write. The mu_novelty_disagree and mu_distortion chains both list this as a step, so chain resources are spent on a no-op. When the outcome verification later checks whether the target metric improved, it will find no change and escalate, wasting the verification window.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Either wire `_prefer_novelty_over_mu` into the stop predicate logic (e.g., in `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` or the FSM event selection), or remove the transform from the chains and replace with one that has actual effect. One option: modify `select_event` in the manager to weight novelty_rate more heavily when this flag is set.

all_findings.description: `_verify_statistical()` in immune_agents.py does not perform any statistical verification. It regex-extracts p-values or correlation coefficients from the claim TEXT and compares them against thresholds. If a claim states "p = 0.03", the function confirms it as significant — but this is circular. It's echoing the claim's own assertion, not independently verifying it. No actual data is tested, no hypothesis test is run, and statsmodels is never imported despite the function docstring and tool_used field claiming otherwise. The function name, docstring, evidence string, and tool_used all misrepresent what happens.

Per-model directive transforms (`add_synthesis_directive`, `add_parsing_directive`, `add_verification_directive`) all gate on `if model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives`. Once any directive is set for a model, no subsequent directive can be added. There is no append, replace, or priority mechanism. A model that received a parsing directive early in the run can never receive a synthesis directive or verification directive later, even if new pathologies are detected. This creates a first-come-first-served directive assignment where the order of pathology detection permanently determines each model's remediation. Over a multi-round run with multiple pathology types, most models become directive-locked after the first remediation.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Append new directives (with length check against `max_per_model_directive_chars` for the combined text), or implement a priority/replacement scheme:
existing = self.config.per_model_directives.get(model_id, "")
combined = f"{existing}\n{directive}" if existing else directive
if len(combined) <= self.config.max_per_model_directive_chars:
    self.config.per_model_directives[model_id] = combined

all_findings.description: `flag_verification_unreliable` transform in `_apply_transform()` sets `self._verification_unreliable_models` (lazily initialized via `hasattr` instead of `__init__`, inconsistent with F008 fix pattern) but no downstream code reads this attribute. The verification_miscalibration remediation chain step 1 flags a model as unreliable, but nothing acts on this flag: finding severity aggregation, convergence detection, and report generation all ignore it. The `verified` field on findings from flagged models is treated identically to verified findings from trusted models. This is similar to IM_F007 (prefer_novelty dead write) — the transform creates state that nothing consumes.

NK Cell anomaly detection checks `f.round_idx > 5` for late-round severity inflation, but default `max_rounds=5` means valid round indices are 0–4 (or at most 0–4 process_round calls). Under default configuration, no finding will ever have `round_idx > 5`, making this check dead code. Even with extended runs, the threshold of 5 is arbitrary and not tied to `config.max_rounds`.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Use a relative threshold based on the configured max_rounds:
late_round_threshold = max(3, int(config.max_rounds * 0.7)) if config else 4
if f.severity > 0.95 and f.round_idx > late_round_threshold:
Or pass `max_rounds` into `nk_cell_verify` and compute the threshold dynamically.

In `DetectorHealthMonitor._verify_remediation_outcomes`, the improvement check for `target_metric == "vocab_growth"` incorrectly uses `old_val` vs `current_val` comparison. The pathology is "vocab_growth below tau_vg", so improvement should be defined as `current_val >= tau_vg`, not `current_val > old_val`. However, if `self._config` is `None`, then `tau_vg` in `_verify_remediation_outcomes` would be `0.04` (from the ternary), but in `record_round` it uses `self._config.tau_vocab_growth` without a fallback, which would raise an `AttributeError`. Actually, in `record_round` there is a guard: `tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth if self._config else 0.04`. So both are consistent. However, there is a deeper issue: the improvement condition for `vocab_growth` should be `current_val >= tau_vg` OR `current_val > old_val`? The pathology is "below tau_vg", so crossing above tau_vg is improvement. But if it's still below tau_vg but increased, is that improvement? The current logic says no. That might be too strict. The fix is to use `current_val >= tau_vg` as improvement, which is already the case. But note that `old_val` is the value when the fix was applied, which was below tau_vg. So if after fix, `current_val` is still below tau_vg but higher than `old_val`, it's not considered improved. That might be okay because the goal is to get it above tau_vg.

However, there is a bug in the `record_round` for vocab_saturation: it uses `self._config.tau_vocab_growth` without checking if `self._config` is `None`. Let's verify:

That's safe.

But in `_verify_remediation_outcomes`, the branch for `target == "vocab_growth"` also uses the same ternary. So it's consistent.

Therefore, the only issue is that the condition `if target in ("mu",):` is a tuple with one element, and it's correct. The `elif` for `vocab_growth` will be executed for `target == "vocab_growth"`. So the code is correct.

Wait, I need to re-examine. The issue is that the `target_metric` passed to `set_remediation_state` is a string, and in `_verify_remediation_outcomes` we have:
if target in ("mu",):
    improved = abs(current_val) < abs(old_val) * 0.95
elif target == "vocab_growth":
    tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth if self._config else 0.04
    improved = current_val >= tau_vg
else:
    improved = current_val > old_val
If `target` is `"vocab_growth"`, then it goes to the `elif` branch. That's correct.

But note: the `target` is set by the remediation chain step. In `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` for `"vocab_saturation"`, the step has `"target_metric": "vocab_growth"`. So it will use the `elif` branch.

Thus, the code is correct. However, there is a bug in the `record_round` for vocab_saturation: the condition for recent_vg is `all(vg < tau_vg for vg in recent_vg)`, and if that's true, it creates a diagnosis. But the remediation chain for `"vocab_saturation"` uses `target_metric: "vocab_growth"`. The improvement condition in `_verify_remediation_outcomes` for `vocab_growth` is `current_val >= tau_vg`. That means if the current vocab_growth is exactly equal to tau_vg, it's considered improved. But the detection condition is `vg < tau_vg` (strictly less). So if after remediation, the vocab_growth becomes exactly tau_vg, it will be considered improved and the pathology will be resolved (since the condition `vg < tau_vg` will be false). That's acceptable.

Therefore, no bug here.

But wait, there is a bug in the `record_round` for vocab_saturation: it uses `self._config.tau_vocab_growth` without checking `self._config` is not None. Actually, it does:
tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth if self._config else 0.04
So it's safe.

Thus, IM_F001 is a false alarm. We need to find a real bug.

Let's look at the `_verify_remediation_outcomes` function again. There is a bug in the `improved` logic for `target == "mu"`. The condition is `abs(current_val) < abs(old_val) * 0.95`. But note that `mu` can be negative. The pathology for mu is "mu increasing while finding count stable/declining". The remediation chain for `"mu_distortion"` has `target_metric: "mu"`. The improvement should be that the distortion is reduced, i.e., the absolute value of mu should decrease (stabilize). So `abs(current_val) < abs(old_val)` is the direction. The 0.95 factor is a 5% improvement threshold. That's correct.

But note: the pathology for mu is about mu increasing, not about absolute value. However, the remediation chain for `"mu_distortion"` is to widen the mu window, which should make the mu metric more stable (closer to zero). So decreasing the absolute value is indeed improvement.

So that seems correct.

Now, let's look at the `record_round` function for mu distortion. The condition for mu increasing is:
mu_increasing = all(
    recent_mu[i + 1] > recent_mu[i] + abs(recent_mu[i]) * 0.1
    for i in range(len(recent_mu) - 1)
)
This is checking if each subsequent mu is greater than the previous by at least 10% of the absolute value of the previous mu. But note that `recent_mu` is a list of mu values. If mu is negative, then `recent_mu[i] + abs(recent_mu[i]) * 0.1` is `recent_mu[i] + |recent_mu[i]|*0.1`. For example, if mu = -5, then threshold = -5 + 5*0.1 = -4.5. The condition `recent_mu[i+1] > -4.5` means mu[i+1] must be greater than -4.5. If mu[i+1] is -4.6, it is less than -4.5, so the condition fails. This is correct because we are looking for increasing mu (becoming less negative). However, note that the pathology is "mu increasing while finding count stable/declining". If mu is negative and becomes less negative (i.e., increases), that's still an increase. So the condition is correct.

But wait, the condition uses `abs(recent_mu[i]) * 0.1` as a margin. This means that if mu is negative and becomes less negative by more than 10% of the absolute value, it's considered increasing. That's acceptable.

Let's formalize:

Goal: mu should stabilize (stop increasing). So improvement is mu stops increasing, i.e., the trend of mu increasing breaks.

The trend check in P-pass should be: if mu is already stabilizing (not increasing), then don't intervene.

But the current trend check uses absolute values. This is wrong.

We need to change the trend check for mu to use the same condition as the pathology detection: check if mu is increasing by at least 10% of absolute value.

However, note that the trend check is for the last 3 rounds. We want to see if the increasing trend has already stopped.

So the condition for mu trend should be: if mu is not increasing (by the same 10% threshold) for the last 3 rounds, then it's improving.

But note that the pathology detection uses a window of `mu_increase_window` (default 2) to detect increasing. The trend check uses 3 rounds. We can use the same condition as the pathology detection but on the last 3 rounds.

Alternatively, we can change the trend check for mu to be: if the absolute value of mu is decreasing (stabilizing), then it's improving. But that might not match the pathology.

mu_increasing = all(
    recent_mu[i + 1] > recent_mu[i] + abs(recent_mu[i]) * 0.1
    for i in range(len(recent_mu) - 1)
)
We can use the same condition for the last 3 mu values.

But note: the trend check is for the last 3 rounds, and we are checking if the metric is already improving. For mu, improving means the increasing trend has stopped. So we should check that there is no increasing trend in the last 3 rounds.

We can define:
if len(history) >= 3:
    recent_3 = history[-3:]
    # Check if mu is increasing in the last 3 rounds
    increasing = all(
        recent_3[i] > recent_3[i-1] + abs(recent_3[i-1]) * 0.1
        for i in range(1, len(recent_3))

    improving = not increasing
But note that the pathology detection uses a window of `mu_increase_window` (default 2) and requires consecutive increases. The trend check for 3 rounds might be too strict. However, the trend check is used to avoid unnecessary intervention. If there is any increasing trend in the last 3 rounds, then intervention might still be needed.

Alternatively, we can use the same condition as the pathology detection but with a window of 3.

But note that the pathology detection window is adaptive (effective window). The trend check is just a simple 3-round window.

Given the complexity, let's note this as a bug and propose a fix.

In `DetectorHealthMonitor._standard_p_pass_remediation` and `_extended_p_pass_remediation`, the trend check for `target_metric == "mu"` uses absolute values to determine improvement. The pathology for mu is "mu increasing while finding count stable/declining", which is about the signed value of mu increasing (becoming less negative or more positive). The current trend check considers the metric improving if the absolute value does not increase by more than 5% over the last 3 rounds. This can incorrectly classify an increasing mu trend as improving if the absolute value is decreasing (e.g., mu is negative and becoming less negative). This may cause the system to skip necessary remediation.

In `immune_agents.py`, function `_parse_ct_output`, the third parsing strategy uses a regex `r'\{[^{}]*"finding_id"[^{}]*\}'` to extract JSON objects from the CT agent's output. This regex does not allow nested braces, but the CT agent's output may contain nested JSON objects (e.g., evidence items). This can cause the parsing to fail, resulting in missing verdicts for the findings.

In `immune_agents.py`, function `_verify_statistical`, the regex for extracting p-value claims only matches `p <= 0.05` or `p=0.05` with the `<=` operator. It does not match `p < 0.05`, `p ≤ 0.05` (unicode), or `p=0.05` without spaces. This may cause the function to miss p-value claims, leading to uncertain verdicts for statistical findings.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Change the regex to `r'p\s*([<=]|≤)?\s*(?:=)?\s*(0\.\d+)'` and capture the operator. Then, if the operator is `<`, `<=`, or `≤`, treat the extracted number as an upper bound for the p-value. If the upper bound is less than or equal to alpha (0.05), then the result is significant. Otherwise, not. If the operator is `=` or missing, treat the extracted number as the exact p-value.

This may cause the system to skip necessary remediation.

In `immune_agents.py`, function `_parse_ct_output`, the third parsing strategy uses a regex `r'\{[^{}]*"finding_id"[^{}]*\}'` to extract JSON objects from the CT agent's output. This regex does not allow nested braces, but the CT agent's output may contain nested JSON objects (e.g., evidence items). This can cause the parsing to fail, resulting in missing verdicts for the findings.

In `immune_agents.py`, function `_verify_statistical`, the regex for extracting p-value claims only matches `p <= 0.05` or `p=0.05` with the `<=` operator. It does not match `p < 0.05`, `p ≤ 0.05` (unicode), or `p=0.05` without spaces. This may cause the function to miss p-value claims, leading to uncertain verdicts for statistical findings.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Change the regex to `r'p\s*([<=]|≤)?\s*(?:=)?\s*(0\.\d+)'` and capture the operator. Then, if the operator is `<`, `<=`, or `≤`, treat the extracted number as an upper bound for the p-value. If the upper bound is less than or equal to alpha (0.05), then the result is significant. Otherwise, not. If the operator is `=` or missing, treat the extracted number as the exact p-value.

all_findings.description: In `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round`, the diagnosis for model_failure sets `pathology_key=f"model_failure_{model_id}"`, but the remediation chain key is `"model_failure"`. This causes a mismatch in the health monitor's state tracking because the remediation state is stored under the chain key (or a key derived from the diagnosis). The health monitor's `_remediation_state` is keyed by the `pathology_key` passed to `set_remediation_state`, which is the chain key. When verifying outcomes, the health monitor looks up the state using the diagnosis's `pathology_key`, which is per-model, but the state is stored under the chain key (without model_id). This leads to missing state and incorrect outcome verification.
all_findings.proposed_fix: In `DynamicManager.apply_diagnosis`, for model_failure, use a composite key for the remediation state that includes the model_id. Specifically, when the chain_key is `"model_failure"`, set `state_key = f"model_failure_{model_id}"` and pass that as `pathology_key` to `set_remediation_state`. The chain key remains `"model_failure"` for looking up the remediation chain steps.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`, damping gate near the start of the method. The code keys damping on `adj["detector"] == diagnosis.detector` plus optional `model_id`. This is wrong for multiple distinct pathologies emitted by the same detector family. Concrete evidence in-scope: both `kappa_stuck` and `monotonic_decline` can emit `diagnosis.detector == "kappa"`-adjacent detector families? More importantly, `check_dispatch_health()` can emit many `detector="verification"` diagnoses for different models, and `record_round()` can emit repeated `detector="mu"`/`detector="mu+novelty"` pathologies with different remediation chains. Damping is specified in comments/config as “same parameter”, but implementation dampens by detector label, not by parameter or chain. This suppresses unrelated safe remediations and violates its own contract.
FIX: Replace detector-based damping with chain/parameter-based damping after chain resolution, and for pre-chain special cases use an explicit synthetic key.
<<<<
        # Check damping: was this parameter adjusted recently?
        # Use composite key (detector + model_id if present) to prevent
        # per-model pathologies from interfering across models (IM_F005).
        diag_model = diagnosis.evidence.get("model_id", "")
        for adj in self._immune_adjustments:
            adj_model = adj.get("model_id", "")
            if (adj["detector"] == diagnosis.detector
                    and adj_model == diag_model
                    and round_idx - adj["round"] < self.config.immune_damping_rounds):
                return None  # Too soon — damping prevents oscillation
====
        # Damping must apply to the same remediation target, not merely the
        # same detector label. detector="verification" can map to distinct
        # models; detector="mu" can emit distinct pathologies. Use a scoped key.
        diag_model = diagnosis.evidence.get("model_id", "")
        damping_key = diagnosis.pathology_key or diagnosis.detector
        if diag_model:
            damping_key = f"{damping_key}:{diag_model}"
        for adj in self._immune_adjustments:
            if (adj.get("damping_key") == damping_key
                    and round_idx - adj["round"] < self.config.immune_damping_rounds):
                return None  # Too soon — damping prevents oscillation
>>>>

And record the key in `_record_adjustment()`:
<<<<
        record = {
            adjustment,
            "detector": diagnosis.detector,
            "round": round_idx,
            "severity": diagnosis.severity,
            "timestamp": time.time(),
        }
====
        diag_model = diagnosis.evidence.get("model_id", "")
        damping_key = diagnosis.pathology_key or diagnosis.detector
        if diag_model:
            damping_key = f"{damping_key}:{diag_model}"
        record = {
            adjustment,
            "detector": diagnosis.detector,
            "round": round_idx,
            "severity": diagnosis.severity,
            "timestamp": time.time(),
            "damping_key": damping_key,
        }
        if diag_model:
            record["model_id"] = diag_model
>>>>
FOLLOW: `approve_deferred_remediation()` currently also dampens by detector only, so it must be updated to use the same `damping_key` logic or it will remain inconsistent with direct AUTO application. No other downstream impact identified.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Scope immune damping by `pathology_key` plus `model_id`, and persist that key in adjustment records so only the same remediation target is damped.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`, branch handling P-pass rejection. When `proceed` is `False`, the code manually writes `self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key]` without `chain_length`. Evidence: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` relies on `state.get("chain_length", 999)` for bounds checking. If a step is P-pass rejected repeatedly, the synthetic state lacks real chain length, so later verification/escalation can create effectively unbounded zombie chains instead of exhausting at the actual chain end.
FIX:
<<<<
            if state:
                state["chain_idx"] = chain_idx + 1
            else:
                self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key] = {
                    "chain_idx": chain_idx + 1,
                    "applied_round": round_idx,
                    "metric_at_apply": current_metric_val,
                    "target_metric": step["target_metric"],
                    "verification_window": 2,
                }
====
            if chain_idx + 1 >= len(chain):
                self.health_monitor.record_chain_exhaustion(chain_key)
                self.health_monitor._remediation_state.pop(chain_key, None)
            elif state:
                state["chain_idx"] = chain_idx + 1
                state["applied_round"] = round_idx
                state["metric_at_apply"] = current_metric_val
                state["target_metric"] = step["target_metric"]
                state["verification_window"] = 2
                state["chain_length"] = len(chain)
            else:
                self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key] = {
                    "chain_idx": chain_idx + 1,
                    "applied_round": round_idx,
                    "metric_at_apply": current_metric_val,
                    "target_metric": step["target_metric"],
                    "verification_window": 2,
                    "chain_length": len(chain),
                }
>>>>
FOLLOW: This changes exhaustion behavior for P-pass-rejected steps from silent indefinite escalation to explicit exhaustion. `self_diagnose()` chain exhaustion metrics will now reflect these cases, which may surface previously hidden chain design weaknesses. That is a desired consequence.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Include real `chain_length` and explicit exhaustion handling when a chain step is skipped due to P-pass rejection.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `approve_deferred_remediation()`. Approved deferred remediations are recorded with `round_idx = deferred["round"]`, i.e. the round when they were queued, not the round when they were actually applied. Evidence: the function computes `current_round = self._process_round_count` for damping, but then ignores it for adjustment logging and `set_remediation_state(applied_round=round_idx)`. This breaks verification windows and audit chronology: a human-approved fix applied later can be evaluated immediately or too early because `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` compares current round to a stale application round.
FIX:
<<<<
        adjustment = self._apply_transform(step["transform"], diag)
        if adjustment:
            round_idx = deferred["round"]
            self._record_adjustment(
                adjustment, diag, round_idx,
                chain_key=deferred["chain_key"],
                chain_idx=deferred["chain_idx"],
            )
            deferred["status"] = "APPROVED"
            current_metric = self._get_current_metric(step["target_metric"])
            # F007 fix: pass chain_length for outcome verification.
            deferred_chain = self._REMEDIATION_CHAINS.get(deferred["chain_key"], [])
            self.health_monitor.set_remediation_state(
                pathology_key=deferred["chain_key"],
                chain_idx=deferred["chain_idx"],
                applied_round=round_idx,
                metric_at_apply=current_metric,
                target_metric=step["target_metric"],
                chain_length=len(deferred_chain),
            )
====
        adjustment = self._apply_transform(step["transform"], diag)
        if adjustment:
            applied_round = current_round
            self._record_adjustment(
                adjustment, diag, applied_round,
                chain_key=deferred["chain_key"],
                chain_idx=deferred["chain_idx"],
            )
            deferred["status"] = "APPROVED"
            deferred["approved_round"] = applied_round
            current_metric = self._get_current_metric(step["target_metric"])
            deferred_chain = self._REMEDIATION_CHAINS.get(deferred["chain_key"], [])
            self.health_monitor.set_remediation_state(
                pathology_key=deferred["chain_key"],
                chain_idx=deferred["chain_idx"],
                applied_round=applied_round,
                metric_at_apply=current_metric,
                target_metric=step["target_metric"],
                chain_length=len(deferred_chain),
            )
>>>>
FOLLOW: Deferred remediation records now need two timestamps semantically: queued round and approved round. Any report consumer using only `deferred["round"]` as “applied” is wrong and should read `approved_round` when present. No other downstream impact identified.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use the actual approval/application round for logging and remediation verification state, and store it separately as `approved_round`.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `record_model_round()`. Per-model pathologies `model_failure_{model_id}`, `parser_yield_{model_id}`, and `cpf_spike_{model_id}` have no resolution path at all. Evidence in code: monotonic decline has an `else` branch that decrements via hysteresis, but the other three only ever increment `_pathology_counts`. This poisons adaptive sensitivity/history, false-positive accounting, and any future recurrence logic because transient per-model incidents never resolve naturally.
FIX: Add explicit hysteretic resolution blocks mirroring `monotonic_decline`.
<<<<
        if consecutive >= 2:
            key = f"model_failure_{model_id}"
            persistence = self._pathology_counts.get(key, 0)
            self._pathology_counts[key] = persistence + 1
            severity = "CRITICAL" if consecutive >= 3 else "WARNING"
            diag = DetectorDiagnosis(
                detector="model_failure",
                pathology=(
                    f"{model_id} has failed {consecutive} consecutive rounds"
                ),
                severity=severity,
                recommended_action=(
                    f"Lower decomposition threshold for {model_id}, or "
                    f"increase timeout, or bench and reassign its workload."
                ),
                evidence={
                    "model_id": model_id,
                    "consecutive_failures": consecutive,
                    "occurrence": persistence + 1,
                },
                pathology_key=f"model_failure_{model_id}",
                round_idx=len(self._kappa_history),
            )
            # DC-1 fix (Run 5): do NOT append to self._diagnoses here.
            # The caller consolidates all diagnoses via record_round().
            results.append(diag)
====
        key = f"model_failure_{model_id}"
        if consecutive >= 2:
            persistence = self._pathology_counts.get(key, 0)
            self._pathology_counts[key] = persistence + 1
            self._resolution_counter[key] = 0
            severity = "CRITICAL" if consecutive >= 3 else "WARNING"
            diag = DetectorDiagnosis(
                detector="model_failure",
                pathology=(
                    f"{model_id} has failed {consecutive} consecutive rounds"
                ),
                severity=severity,
                recommended_action=(
                    f"Lower decomposition threshold for {model_id}, or "
                    f"increase timeout, or bench and reassign its workload."
                ),
                evidence={
                    "model_id": model_id,
                    "consecutive_failures": consecutive,
                    "occurrence": persistence + 1,
                },
                pathology_key=f"model_failure_{model_id}",
                round_idx=len(self._kappa_history),
            )
            results.append(diag)
        elif self._pathology_counts.get(key, 0) > 0:
            self._resolution_counter[key] = self._resolution_counter.get(key, 0) + 1
            hysteresis = getattr(self._config, "resolution_hysteresis", 2)
            if self._resolution_counter[key] >= hysteresis:
                self._resolved_counts[key] = self._resolved_counts.get(key, 0) + 1
                if key not in self._remediation_state:
                    self.record_natural_resolution(key)
                self._pathology_counts[key] = 0
                self._resolution_counter[key] = 0
>>>>

Apply the same pattern to `parser_yield_{model_id}` and `cpf_spike_{model_id}` with their respective non-pathological conditions:
- parser_yield resolves when `not (response_chars > tau_chars and finding_count == 0 and not failed)`
- cpf_spike resolves when the spike condition is false after enough rounds.
FOLLOW: Once natural resolution is recorded for these per-model keys, `false_positive_rate` will increase for transient per-model anomalies. That may trigger self-diagnosis more often; this is behaviorally correct but exposes that false-positive accounting mixes heterogeneous pathology types in one pool. No additional fix asserted here.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Add resolution-hysteresis handling for all per-model pathologies that currently only accumulate counts.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `check_dispatch_health()`, dispatch false-positive detection. The loop diagnoses a block as false-positive if `any(s > block_round for s in successes)`. That is unbounded in time and ignores causal proximity. A model blocked in round 0 and succeeding naturally in round 4 still triggers a “false positive” diagnosis, despite the comment specifying “round R but succeeded in round R+1 via decomposition.” This is a correctness bug, not documentation only, because it creates spurious immune remediations.
FIX:
<<<<
                if any(s > block_round for s in successes):
====
                if (block_round + 1) in successes:
>>>>

Optionally tighten evidence text accordingly:
<<<<
                                f"at round {block_round} but succeeded later "
                                f"via decomposition"
====
                                f"at round {block_round} but succeeded in round "
                                f"{block_round + 1} via decomposition"
>>>>
FOLLOW: This reduces diagnosis volume for `dispatch_false_positive`, which also reduces automatic additions to `pre_decompose_models`. Any experiment baselines expecting the broader historical behavior will shift, but toward the documented contract. No further downstream impact identified.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Restrict dispatch false-positive detection to immediate next-round recovery, matching the stated contract.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`, special-case advisory branch for `mu_novelty_disagree`. The branch returns after logging an adjustment-like record without setting remediation state, despite a remediation chain existing for `mu_novelty_disagree` in `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`. This is distinct from the previously known “bypasses chain mechanism” finding because the code now still contains the bypass after chain definitions were added, creating a concrete dead chain: step 1 (`widen_mu_window`) is unreachable forever, and outcome verification can never confirm or escalate the advisory.
FIX:
<<<<
        elif diagnosis.pathology_key == "mu_novelty_disagree" or (
            not diagnosis.pathology_key and diagnosis.detector == "mu+novelty"
            and "disagree" in diagnosis.pathology.lower()
        ):
            # Advisory — no parameter to adjust
            adjustment = {
                "parameter": "stop_signal_priority",
                "old": "mu+novelty combined",
                "new": "novelty_rate preferred (mu unreliable)",
                "reason": diagnosis.pathology,
            }
            self._record_adjustment(adjustment, diagnosis, round_idx)
            return adjustment
====
        elif diagnosis.pathology_key == "mu_novelty_disagree" or (
            not diagnosis.pathology_key and diagnosis.detector == "mu+novelty"
            and "disagree" in diagnosis.pathology.lower()
        ):
            chain_key = "mu_novelty_disagree"
>>>>
FOLLOW: With the bypass removed, `_apply_transform("prefer_novelty", ...)` is now used. That exposes the already-known dormant-transform issue more often if `_prefer_novelty_over_mu` remains unread downstream. The chain will at least escalate correctly now, but the transform consumer still needs to exist for behavioral effect.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Route `mu_novelty_disagree` through its remediation chain instead of returning from a special-case advisory branch.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `run_immune_pipeline()`, parallel collection loop. All futures use `future.result(timeout=ct_timeout + 30)`, including B-Cell and NK-Cell tasks that should be fast and local. Because iteration is insertion-ordered and CT is submitted first, a hung CT consumes the full long timeout before the code even observes already-finished B/NK results. This is an immune integration latency bug: one network-bound cell delays all local verification outputs, defeating the stated staged architecture.
FIX:
<<<<
        for name, future in futures.items():
            try:
                result = future.result(timeout=ct_timeout + 30)
====
        per_cell_timeout = {
            "cytotoxic_t": ct_timeout + 30,
            "b_cell": 30,
            "nk_cell": 30,
        }
        for name, future in futures.items():
            try:
                result = future.result(timeout=per_cell_timeout.get(name, 30))
>>>>
A stronger exact fix is to use `concurrent.futures.as_completed`, but the above is the minimal replacement.
FOLLOW: This does not fully decouple wall-clock completion order because iteration remains ordered; if CT is first and times out at `ct_timeout+30`, later completed futures are still processed late. The complete fix is:
- iterate with `as_completed(futures.values())`
- map futures back to names.
That is the next required refinement if latency isolation matters.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use per-cell timeouts at minimum; preferably collect futures with `as_completed` so CT delays do not block local B/NK results.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `approve_deferred_remediation()`. The recreated `DetectorDiagnosis` omits `pathology_key` and `round_idx`, even though these fields are used elsewhere for routing, damping, and audit-window logic. Evidence: the constructor only passes detector/pathology/severity/recommended_action/evidence. This creates interface drift between direct diagnoses and approved deferred diagnoses; any transform or logger depending on `pathology_key` loses information on the deferred path.
FIX:
<<<<
        diag = DetectorDiagnosis(
            detector=deferred["diagnosis"]["detector"],
            pathology=deferred["diagnosis"]["pathology"],
            severity=deferred["diagnosis"]["severity"],
            recommended_action=step["description"],
            evidence=deferred["diagnosis"].get("evidence", {}),
        )
====
        diag = DetectorDiagnosis(
            detector=deferred["diagnosis"]["detector"],
            pathology=deferred["diagnosis"]["pathology"],
            severity=deferred["diagnosis"]["severity"],
            recommended_action=step["description"],
            evidence=deferred["diagnosis"].get("evidence", {}),
            pathology_key=deferred["chain_key"],
            round_idx=current_round,
        )
>>>>
FOLLOW: Combined with IM_F001, this ensures deferred approvals share the same damping and logging semantics as direct applications. No downstream impact identified.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Preserve `pathology_key` and actual `round_idx` when reconstructing diagnoses for deferred approvals.

all_findings.description:
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `process_round()`, regression handling block just after dispatch-health monitoring. The code evaluates candidate regressions using `self._pre_fix_snapshots`, then immediately truncates that list to only snapshots with `round_idx - s["round"] < 2`, and only after that computes `regression_this_round` for clearing `_regression_defer`. Evidence: the reset logic is:

- cleanup:
  `self._pre_fix_snapshots = [s for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots if round_idx - s["round"] < 2]`
- then:
  `regression_this_round = any(round_idx - s["round"] >= 2 ... for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots)`

These predicates are mutually exclusive, so `regression_this_round` is always `False`. That means `_healthy_rounds_since_regression` increments even in rounds where an old snapshot just produced a regression signal, and `_regression_defer` can clear too early. This is a missed immune-behaviour bug because it breaks the safety latch that gates future autonomous remediations.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
FIX:
<<<<
        # --- Regression detection (Exp15) ---
        # Check if any AUTO fix made metrics worse.  If a fix caused a
        # regression (target metric declined AND another metric dropped
        # significantly), log and defer future fixes for human review.
        if self._pre_fix_snapshots and round_idx >= 2:
            for snap in self._pre_fix_snapshots:
                if round_idx - snap["round"] < 2:
                    continue  # too early to judge
                current_metrics = {
                    "kappa": self._get_current_metric("kappa"),
                    "mu": self._get_current_metric("mu"),
                    "finding_count": self._get_current_metric("finding_count"),
                    "vocab_growth": self._get_current_metric("vocab_growth"),
                }
                pre_metrics = snap["metrics"]
                # Check for regression: finding_count dropped by >30%
                pre_fc = pre_metrics.get("finding_count", 0)
                cur_fc = current_metrics.get("finding_count", 0)
                if pre_fc > 0 and cur_fc < pre_fc * 0.7:
                    self.event_stream.emit(
                        ManagerEvent(
                            event_type=ManagerEventType.STOP_CHECK,
                            model_id="system",
                            round_idx=round_idx,
                            detail=(
                                f"[IMMUNE:REGRESSION] Fix at round {snap['round']} "
                                f"({snap['chain_key']} step {snap['chain_idx']}) "
                                f"may have caused regression: finding_count "
                                f"{pre_fc:.0f} → {cur_fc:.0f} (-{(1-cur_fc/pre_fc)*100:.0f}%). "
                                f"Deferring further autonomous fixes for human review."
                            ),
                            metadata={
                                "regression": True,
                                "pre_fix": pre_metrics,
                                "post_fix": current_metrics,
                                "fix_round": snap["round"],
                            },
                        )
                    )
                    # PR-3 fix: set regression defer flag
                    self._regression_defer = True
            # Clean up checked snapshots
            self._pre_fix_snapshots = [
                s for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots
                if round_idx - s["round"] < 2
            ]

        # F005 fix: reset regression defer after resolution_hysteresis
        # consecutive healthy rounds (no regression detected). The one-way
        # latch otherwise permanently blocks autonomous remediation.
        if self._regression_defer:
            # If no regression was detected this round, increment healthy counter
            regression_this_round = any(
                round_idx - s["round"] >= 2
                and s.get("metrics", {}).get("finding_count", 0) > 0
                and self._get_current_metric("finding_count")
                < s["metrics"].get("finding_count", 0) * 0.7
                for s in self._pre_fix_snapshots
            )
            if not regression_this_round:
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression += 1
            else:
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression = 0
            if self._healthy_rounds_since_regression >= self.config.resolution_hysteresis:
                self._regression_defer = False
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression = 0
====
        # --- Regression detection (Exp15) ---
        # Check if any AUTO fix made metrics worse.  If a fix caused a
        # regression (target metric declined AND another metric dropped
        # significantly), log and defer future fixes for human review.
        regression_this_round = False
        if self._pre_fix_snapshots and round_idx >= 2:
            remaining_snapshots: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            current_metrics = {
                "kappa": self._get_current_metric("kappa"),
                "mu": self._get_current_metric("mu"),
                "finding_count": self._get_current_metric("finding_count"),
                "vocab_growth": self._get_current_metric("vocab_growth"),
            }

            for snap in self._pre_fix_snapshots:
                if round_idx - snap["round"] < 2:
                    remaining_snapshots.append(snap)
                    continue  # too early to judge

                pre_metrics = snap["metrics"]
                # Check for regression: finding_count dropped by >30%
                pre_fc = pre_metrics.get("finding_count", 0)
                cur_fc = current_metrics.get("finding_count", 0)
                if pre_fc > 0 and cur_fc < pre_fc * 0.7:
                    regression_this_round = True
                    self.event_stream.emit(
                        ManagerEvent(
                            event_type=ManagerEventType.STOP_CHECK,
                            model_id="system",
                            round_idx=round_idx,
                            detail=(
                                f"[IMMUNE:REGRESSION] Fix at round {snap['round']} "
                                f"({snap['chain_key']} step {snap['chain_idx']}) "
                                f"may have caused regression: finding_count "
                                f"{pre_fc:.0f} → {cur_fc:.0f} (-{(1-cur_fc/pre_fc)*100:.0f}%). "
                                f"Deferring further autonomous fixes for human review."
                            ),
                            metadata={
                                "regression": True,
                                "pre_fix": pre_metrics,
                                "post_fix": current_metrics,
                                "fix_round": snap["round"],
                            },
                        )
                    )
                    # PR-3 fix: set regression defer flag
                    self._regression_defer = True

            # Clean up checked snapshots
            self._pre_fix_snapshots = remaining_snapshots

        # F005 fix: reset regression defer after resolution_hysteresis
        # consecutive healthy rounds (no regression detected). The one-way
        # latch otherwise permanently blocks autonomous remediation.
        if self._regression_defer:
            if not regression_this_round:
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression += 1
            else:
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression = 0
            if self._healthy_rounds_since_regression >= self.config.resolution_hysteresis:
                self._regression_defer = False
                self._healthy_rounds_since_regression = 0
>>>>

all_findings.description: FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `approve_deferred_remediation()`. The damping check for deferred approvals ignores the per-model scoping used elsewhere and can wrongly block approval of a deferred remediation for one model because a different model had a recent adjustment with the same detector. Evidence: `apply_diagnosis()` already uses both `diagnosis.detector` and `diagnosis.evidence["model_id"]` when enforcing damping, but `approve_deferred_remediation()` checks only `adj.get("detector") == deferred["diagnosis"]["detector"]`. In `bench/immune_agents.py`, `_verify_z3()` always produces `SATISFIABLE_COUNTEREXAMPLE` (→ REJECTED verdict) for any if/then claim. The code creates unconstrained booleans `X = z3.Bool('X'); Y = z3.Bool('Y')`, then checks `s.add(X); s.add(z3.Not(Y))`. Since X and Y are free variables, `X=True, Y=False` is always a satisfying assignment. The semantic content of the claim is never encoded — the z3 solver sees generic booleans, not the actual conditions from the finding. Every logical if/then finding is systematically rejected regardless of validity. This corrupts B-Cell verdicts for all LOGICAL claim types, which then feed into Helper T confidence-weighted voting and bias the pipeline toward false rejection of valid logical findings.
all_findings.proposed_fix: The z3 verification for if/then claims needs to encode the actual constraint semantics, not unconstrained booleans. As a minimum viable fix: change the if/then handler to return UNCERTAIN with low confidence instead of a misleading REJECTED, and add a comment documenting that structured z3 encoding requires claim-specific parsing. Longer term: parse numeric constraints from both sides of the if/then and encode them as z3 arithmetic constraints, or remove the if/then branch entirely and fall back to UNCERTAIN.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`: when `_apply_transform()` returns None (transform had no effect — e.g., model already has a directive, or parameter already at floor), no remediation state is set and the chain index is never advanced. On the next round (after damping expires), `apply_diagnosis()` reads `chain_idx=0` from the empty remediation state and retries the same ineffective transform. This creates a silent infinite retry loop. Concretely: `add_parsing_directive`, `add_verification_directive`, and `add_synthesis_directive` all guard with `if model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives` — once any directive exists for a model, all subsequent directive-based transforms return None, locking that chain step forever. Similarly, `lower_tau_sim_01` returns None when tau_sim is already at floor 0.3, preventing escalation to step 2.
all_findings.proposed_fix: When `_apply_transform()` returns None, treat it as "transform inapplicable" and advance the chain index without setting verification state. Add to `apply_diagnosis()` after the `if adjustment:` block: `else: state = self.health_monitor._remediation_state.get(chain_key, {}); next_idx = chain_idx + 1; if next_idx < len(chain): self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key] = {"chain_idx": next_idx, ...}; else: self.health_monitor.record_chain_exhaustion(chain_key)`. For directives specifically, change the guard to append/merge rather than skip when a directive already exists.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `record_model_round()`: three per-model pathology types — `cpf_spike`, `parser_yield`, and `model_failure` — have detection logic that increments `self._pathology_counts[key]` but lack resolution paths. Compare with `monotonic_decline`, which has an `else` branch that uses `_resolution_counter` and hysteresis to clear pathology counts when the condition resolves. For `cpf_spike`, there is no code path that decrements or clears the count when CPF returns to normal. For `parser_yield`, no resolution when the model starts producing findings again. For `model_failure`, `_model_failure_counts` resets to 0 on success but `_pathology_counts[f"model_failure_{model_id}"]` never clears. Consequences: (a) adaptive sensitivity via `effective_window()` only ever narrows for these pathologies, never recovering baseline; (b) `record_natural_resolution()` is never called, so `false_positive_rate` understates transient pathologies; (c) severity escalation is one-way (persistence count only grows).
all_findings.proposed_fix: Add resolution paths in `record_model_round()` for each missing pathology, mirroring the `monotonic_decline` pattern: when the pathological condition is no longer met, increment `_resolution_counter[key]`, and when it reaches `resolution_hysteresis`, clear `_pathology_counts[key]`, call `record_natural_resolution(key)`, and reset counters.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `process_round()`: the regression-defer reset logic at ~line "F005 fix" always resets after `resolution_hysteresis` rounds because it can never detect an ongoing regression. The snapshot cleanup immediately above removes all snapshots where `round_idx - s["round"] >= 2`. The subsequent regression check filters with `round_idx - s["round"] >= 2`, which matches zero snapshots (they were just removed). Therefore `regression_this_round` is always `False`, `_healthy_rounds_since_regression` always increments, and `_regression_defer` always clears after `resolution_hysteresis` rounds regardless of whether the regression actually resolved. The F005 fix defeats itself because it reads the same data structure that was just cleaned.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Move the regression-defer reset check BEFORE the snapshot cleanup block, or use a separate boolean flag set during the regression detection loop (e.g., `regression_detected_this_round = True` inside the loop) and reference that flag in the defer-reset logic instead of re-scanning the cleaned snapshot list.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`: when the P-pass rejects a fix (`proceed=False`), the `else` branch creates a new `_remediation_state` entry with `applied_round`, `metric_at_apply`, and `verification_window` — as though a fix was actually applied. `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` will later check this state, compare the metric against `metric_at_apply`, and produce a verdict. If the metric didn't improve (likely, since nothing was applied), it emits "Remediation INEFFECTIVE" and escalates the chain — this is correct behaviour (skip to next step) but the audit log records a false outcome for a never-applied fix. If the metric improved naturally, it records "Remediation SUCCESSFUL" and credits the non-existent application — a false positive in the remediation log that corrupts Level 3 self-assessment (`remediation_success_rate`, `_step_effectiveness`).
all_findings.proposed_fix: When P-pass rejects and no state exists, only store the chain index advancement without verification metadata: `self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key] = {"chain_idx": chain_idx + 1, "applied_round": -1, "skip_verification": True, ...}`. In `_verify_remediation_outcomes`, skip entries with `skip_verification=True`.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`: for `target_metric == "vocab_growth"`, improvement is defined as `current_val >= tau_vg` where `tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth`. But the `vocab_saturation` remediation chain's step 0 (`halve_tau_vocab`) HALVES `tau_vocab_growth` before the verification window elapses. After the first fix (0.04 → 0.02), the verification check becomes `current_val >= 0.02` instead of `current_val >= 0.04`. The remediation declares success even though actual vocab growth hasn't changed — the threshold moved under it. This creates a false-success cycle: detect saturation → halve threshold → declare success (metric now above new threshold) → clear pathology → detect again at old rate → repeat. The fix should compare against the threshold that was in effect when the pathology was first detected, not the current (already-adjusted) threshold.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Store the `tau_vg` value at detection time in `set_remediation_state()` and use that stored value in the verification check. Add `"threshold_at_apply": tau_vg` to the remediation state dict and use it: `improved = current_val >= state.get("threshold_at_apply", tau_vg)`.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `process_round()`: per-model diagnoses from `health_monitor.record_model_round()` are immediately passed to `apply_diagnosis()`, which calls `_get_current_metric()` for P-pass evaluation. But at this point, `health_monitor.record_round()` has not yet been called — `_kappa_history`, `_mu_history`, `_novelty_history`, and `_finding_counts` still reflect the PREVIOUS round's values. System-level diagnoses from `record_round()` (processed later) correctly use current-round values. This means the P-pass trend check ("Is the metric already improving?") uses stale data for per-model remediations, potentially vetoing valid fixes or approving invalid ones based on outdated metrics. The inconsistency is systematic: every per-model pathology (model_failure, parser_yield, monotonic_decline, cpf_spike) is P-passed against the wrong round's data.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Defer `apply_diagnosis()` calls for per-model diagnoses until after `record_round()` completes and metric histories are updated. Collect per-model diagnoses in a list, then process them alongside system-level diagnoses after the `record_round()` call.

all_findings.description: `_finding_similarity()`, `_tokenize_for_similarity()`, and `_bigrams()` are identically duplicated in `bench/dm/_manager.py` and `bench/dm/_convergence.py`. `immune_agents.py` imports from `_convergence`. `DynamicManager.update_fingerprints()` uses the `_manager.py` copy. `ConvergenceDetector` uses the `_convergence.py` copy. If either copy is modified independently (e.g., a bug fix applied to one but not the other), similarity scores will silently diverge between convergence detection and fingerprint updates, causing inconsistent kappa and D_decay calculations from the same finding pairs. This already occurred in the codebase history: the `_STOPWORDS` frozenset is also duplicated, doubling maintenance surface.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Remove the duplicate from `_manager.py` and import `_finding_similarity` from `bench.dm._convergence` (as `immune_agents.py` already does). The `_manager.py` module already imports from `_convergence` indirectly via `_types`, so adding a direct import creates no new dependency.

all_findings.description: In `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose` method, the adjustment for high false positive rate increases `sensitivity_decay` (line: `new_decay = min(0.95, old_decay + 0.05)`). This is incorrect because in `effective_window`, the decay factor is used as `decay  (-resolved)`. Increasing decay makes this term smaller, which narrows the effective window (making the detector more sensitive). The goal when false positive rate is high is to reduce sensitivity (widen the window).
all_findings.proposed_fix: Decrease `sensitivity_decay` instead of increasing it, with a floor to avoid extreme values.

FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `recommended_chain_start()`. The function is intended to “skip step 0 next time” when earlier steps have repeatedly failed and later steps have succeeded, but its loop returns the first non-skipped index in numeric order, not the first historically effective step after the failed prefix. Evidence: if step 0 has 2 fails/0 success and step 1 has 1 success, the code sets `last_skipped = 0`, continues, then on `idx = 1` immediately returns `1`; that case works. But if both step 0 and step 1 are historically ineffective and step 2 has succeeded, it returns `2` only because both were skipped. `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`: when `_apply_transform()` returns `None` (parameter already at its target value — a no-op), no `set_remediation_state()` is called, no adjustment is recorded, and `chain_idx` never advances. Combined with the Run 10 `tau_sim` default change from 0.8 to 0.33: `lower_tau_sim_01` moves tau_sim from 0.33 to `max(0.3, 0.23)` = 0.3 on first application (works once). The entire `kappa_stuck` chain is permanently stalled after one successful application — all three steps are no-ops, but the chain never registers exhaustion because `_apply_transform` returns `None` and `apply_diagnosis` silently exits.
all_findings.proposed_fix: When `_apply_transform` returns `None`, check whether the parameter is already at the chain step's target value. If so, advance `chain_idx` in `_remediation_state` to skip the no-op step, or record chain exhaustion if no further steps exist. all_findings.description: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`: the vocab_growth improvement check reads `tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth` at verification time, but the `halve_tau_vocab` transform already modified this value when the remediation was applied. Trace: round R detects vocab_saturation, applies `halve_tau_vocab` (tau_vg 0.04 → 0.02), records `metric_at_apply = 0.03`. Round R+2 verifies: `current_val = 0.03`, `improved = 0.03 >= 0.02` → True. all_findings.description: FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, constructor comment block for adaptive immune response and the adjacent `effective_window()` implementation. The formal documentation still contradicts the code. Evidence: the docstring says repeated exposure to the same pathology “narrows the window and speeds response,” but the formal block defines `W_d(r) = W_d(0) · decay^(count_resolved_d) + growth · count_persistent_d`, with annotations claiming `decay` shrinks after false alarms and `growth` grows after persistent true positives. The actual code does the opposite structure: `widen = decay  (-resolved)` and `narrow = 1.0 / (1.0 + growth * persistent)`. The comments above `effective_window()` are therefore stale and mathematically wrong. This is in-scope documentation because the immune layer is explicitly adaptive and self-verifying.

FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`, direct special-case branch for `verification_miscalibration`. The branch writes a per-model directive directly and returns, bypassing `_apply_transform("add_verification_directive")`. Evidence: `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS["verification_miscalibration"]` step 0 is already defined as `add_verification_directive`, but the special case duplicates similar-but-not-identical directive text and skips the transform interface entirely. This creates interface drift: chain metadata says one transform is being used, while actual application uses ad hoc code. It also bypasses any future fixes made inside `_apply_transform("add_verification_directive")`, making the chain declaration misleading.

FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`, P-pass invocation for single-model transforms. The code always passes `affected_model_ids = [m.model_id for m in self.models]` into `health_monitor.p_pass_remediation(...)`, regardless of whether the transform affects one model or all models. Evidence: per-model chain steps such as `add_parsing_directive`, `add_verification_directive`, and `add_to_pre_decompose` operate on `diagnosis.evidence["model_id"]` only, but extended P-pass classification consumes `affected_models` to assess cascade risk and over-specification. Supplying the full model pool causes false multi-model scope in the adversarial pass, inflating risks like “fix affects 3+ models simultaneously” for fixes that touch only one model. This is a logic bug in immune P-pass scoping.

FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `check_dispatch_health()`, verification miscalibration recovery branch. When a model recovers, the code resets `_pathology_counts[key]` and `_resolution_counter[key]` but does not record a resolution event. Evidence: other pathology resolution paths in `record_round()` increment `_resolved_counts[...]` and call `record_natural_resolution(...)` when no remediation is active. Here, the miscalibration branch omits both, so adaptive sensitivity and false-positive accounting never learn from recovered verification pathologies. Because `false_positive_rate` is one of the self-diagnosis triggers, this omission undercounts natural resolutions in an in-scope immune feedback loop.

FIND: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `_verify_sympy()`. The numerical fallback blindly substitutes `n=100` into `expr` even when the parsed expression is not symbolic in `n` or is not substitution-safe. Evidence: after `result = sympy.simplify(expr)`, the code executes `n_val = expr.subs(symbols('n'), 100)` for every non-boolean result. For expressions without `n`, this does nothing; for inequalities or partially symbolic forms it can still leave a non-boolean expression; for claims using different variable names, the fallback provides a false aura of numeric checking while actually testing nothing relevant. This is an edge-case verification bug in the B-cell pipeline.

FIND: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `run_immune_pipeline()`, result collection loop over futures. The loop waits on each future in submission order with `future.result(timeout=ct_timeout + 30)`, so a slow CT task can delay collection of already-completed B-cell and NK-cell results. Evidence: `cytotoxic_t` is submitted first, then `b_cell`, then `nk_cell`; iteration over `futures.items()` preserves insertion order. If CT blocks near the timeout, the loop will not consume B-cell or NK outputs until after that wait, even though they are local and typically fast. This needlessly serialises the parallel stage and can stretch wall-clock latency.

FIND: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `_parse_ct_output()`, Strategy 3 regex extraction. The fallback regex `r'\\{[^{}]*\"finding_id\"[^{}]*\\}'` cannot extract JSON objects containing nested braces, which CT verdicts naturally include because each item may carry an `evidence` array of objects. Evidence from the same file: `_ct_evidence_to_verdict()` expects each raw CT verdict to have `evidence_items=rv.get("evidence", [])`, and each evidence item is itself a dict with `file`, `line`, `code_snippet`, `observation`. Such nested JSON cannot be matched by `[^{}]*`. Therefore the mixed-text fallback silently drops precisely the structured outputs it needs most.
